01 / HOW IT WORKS

How the engine
creates a graph.

Inputs reveal entities, relationships and observations. Projections provide views of that evidence.

01Bring dataCloud resources · flows · logs · telemetry
→
02InterpretExtract topology · read signals · correlate
→
03Project graphsMatch · transform · combine · propagate
→
04Explore changeViews · graph diffs · history
TOPOLOGY + SIGNALS

Connect signals to the system.

Cloud resources, network flows, telemetry and logs can each contribute entities, relationships and signals. Available evidence determines coverage.

KubernetesNetwork flowsHTTPML logs

The engine may use Quine, Cypher or Memgraph internally. Their roles in the implementation remain open.

COMPOSABLE PROJECTIONS

Transform one graph into many.

A projection is a graph-based configuration. Like XSLT for graphs, it defines a transformation. Projections can combine source data, graphs and graph diffs; their outputs can feed other projections.

INPUT GRAPH→PROJECTION→OUTPUT + DIFF

For a new format, AI can propose a mapping rule. Replay uses a fixed rule, input order, prior state and time schedule. Independent changes may arrive in either order.

ATTRIBUTE PROPAGATION

Propagate attributes.

Rules determine what travels, where it travels and how values combine.

CoreDNS signals can inform Cluster DNS. The projection uses the input evidence to determine any effect on the capability.

03 / MODEL

Define identity,
types and views.

The model distinguishes identity, ontology and projection.

◎

Timeless identity

Identity is timeless. A projection selects fields that establish the identity of its entities.

◈

Versioned ontology

Types, relationships and properties have meaning within an ontology version.

⌘

Graph projections

Each projection is a configuration graph. It produces a separate output graph and change events.

SAME INPUTS / DIFFERENT PROJECTIONS

Which fields define identity?

Each projection selects the fields it uses. Here, two pod records can produce two pod entities or one deployment entity.

INPUT RECORDS
Pod AUID: pod-a · deployment: checkout
Pod BUID: pod-b · deployment: checkout
→IDENTITY FIELDpod UID→
OUTPUT ENTITIES
pod-apod-b

Two UID values → two pod entities.
